d: The Beauty Advisor is responsible for representing the brand by maximizing sales within the store through exceptional customer service and deep product knowledge. This role involves creating a welcoming environment, providing personalized beauty consultations, and contributing to the overall store operations and visual presentation standards as directed by the store manager or assistant store manager.
q: Strong knowledge of cosmetics, skincare, and beauty trends with experience in applying products. Proven customer service skills in retail, especially in beauty, and ability to build rapport with customers. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills for personalized product recommendations. A background in cosmetology or skincare is preferred but not mandatory; professional training in makeup or skincare is a plus.
r: Serve as the initial point of contact for customers, offering personalized beauty consultations and product recommendations tailored to individual needs.
Engage with customers in a warm, approachable manner, providing skincare advice, makeup tutorials, and product demonstrations to enhance the shopping experience.
Assist customers in selecting products that meet their specific beauty needs, converting window shoppers into buyers, and building lasting customer relationships.
Proactively promote and upsell the brand’s products, including cross-selling complementary items from within the store or other group brands.
Promote and encourage customers to join the Club Apparel Loyalty Program to drive repeat sales and brand loyalty.
Stay updated on the latest beauty trends, product launches, and ingredients in skincare and makeup to provide accurate information to customers.
Maintain a deep understanding of the brand’s ethos, heritage, and products to deliver a consistent and compelling message to customers.
Ensure that personal grooming and appearance reflect the brand image at all times.
Demonstrate and apply makeup or skincare products to showcase their features and benefits, ensuring customers leave with a positive and informed impression of the brand.
Assist in store operational tasks, including opening and closing procedures, inventory management, and stock replenishment to ensure a well-stocked and organized sales floor.
Help maintain visual presentation standards and ensure the store is clean, organized, and visually appealing according to company guidelines.
Support in executing marketing and promotional activities, such as in-store events or product launches, to enhance customer engagement.
Follow Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) in handling payments, product returns, and customer complaints professionally and efficiently.
Ensure compliance with health and safety standards, particularly when handling beauty products.
Consistently achieve or exceed individual sales targets, contributing to the overall store’s performance.
Track and report on key performance indicators (KPIs) such as conversion rates, average transaction values, and customer satisfaction scores.
Work closely with the team to meet collective goals, supporting a collaborative and results-driven store environment.

d: Riyadh University of Arts (RUA) is a newly established institution dedicated to arts education, creative practice, and cultural development in Saudi Arabia. As part of the Kingdom's Vision 2030 initiative, RUA is being developed as a national centre for arts education and a driver of the country's growing cultural and creative sectors.

RUA brings together academic and industry expertise to deliver practice-based, interdisciplinary programmes that prepare students for careers in the creative economy. The University is designed to serve as a regional and global hub for cultural exchange, supporting collaboration between artists, scholars, and industry partners.
About the College of Theatre and Performing Arts

The College of Theatre and Performing Arts is dedicated to shaping the future of theatre and performing arts in Saudi Arabia by developing bold, imaginative, and culturally connected artists whose work moves audiences at home and across the world. Through ambitious, practice-led education, students take creative risks, discover their artistic voice, and learn through making, collaboration, performance, and reflection. Rooted in Saudi culture and connected to regional and international practice, the College brings together artistic excellence, interdisciplinary collaboration, professional practice, and research.

The College's inaugural programme, the BA in Acting (Theatre & Film), is a four-year undergraduate programme delivered in partnership with AMDA College of the Performing Arts, reflecting international standards. From 2027/28 the College is expanding its offer, and its programmes will cover the following areas of specialism:

The College of Theatre and Performing Arts at RUA is seeking full-time faculty for the 2027/28 academic year, with a planned joining date of 1 August 2027. Positions are available in each of the College's areas of specialism listed above. Appointments are open rank, depending on qualifications, experience, and professional standing.

Candidates should identify the specialism for which they wish to be considered. The areas below describe the expertise sought across the faculty team; individual candidates are not expected to cover every area.
Acting techniques and actor training methodologies; scene study, textual analysis and rehearsal practice
Devising, improvisation and ensemble-based performance; classical and contemporary acting practices
Screen acting techniques and performance for film and television, including on-camera scene work
Screen rehearsal, continuity, performance for camera and actor–director collaboration
Dance technique, training methodologies and pedagogy across contemporary and other dance forms
Traditional, folk and culturally specific dance practices, including Saudi, Middle Eastern and international traditions
Physical theatre, somatic practice, movement analysis, dance science, physical conditioning and safe practice
Choreographic practice, composition, movement direction and original performance-making
Improvisation, devising, ensemble-based creation and interdisciplinary performance
Performer health and wellbeing, physical preparation and responsible rehearsal practice
Theatre directing, directorial methodologies, rehearsal practice, actor–director collaboration and artistic leadership
Artistic direction of live events, festivals, ceremonies and large-scale productions, including devised, site-specific and interdisciplinary performance
Dramaturgical theory, production dramaturgy, textual and performance analysis, and research
Rehearsal dramaturgy, collaborative theatre-making and contemporary or non-text-based performance
Playwriting, dramatic structure, script development, adaptation and new writing
Collaborative development of original dramatic work and postgraduate creative or research-led projects
q: MFA or Master's degree in Theatre, Performing Arts, Acting, Directing, Dramaturgy, Choreography, or a closely related discipline, or substantial professional credits
Documented experience teaching at university level or in a conservatoire or professional training environment
A strong professional portfolio in the specialist area
For appointment at Associate Professor or Professor level: an established record of professional, scholarly, or creative achievement appropriate to the rank
PhD, MFA, or DFA in Theatre or Performing Arts, or equivalent professional experience
Experience teaching within conservatoire-style training programmes
Experience working across theatre, film, and recorded media
r: Faculty members will contribute to the delivery and development of the College's practice-based curriculum. Responsibilities will include:
Deliver high-quality studio-based teaching, workshops, and rehearsal-based classes
Supervise and mentor student productions, performances, and creative projects through to final presentation and assessment
Assess student work and provide constructive formative and summative feedback
Contribute to assessment design, moderation, curriculum development and academic quality assurance
Support students' artistic, technical, and professional development through structured practice and mentorship
Provide academic tutorials, monitor student progress and offer appropriate academic guidance
Collaborate with faculty colleagues and technical staff to support integrated programme delivery
Participate in auditions, admissions interviews, portfolio reviews and applicant assessment
Maintain a safe, inclusive, and professional learning environment
In addition, faculty will be expected to contribute to programme development, student recruitment, and the broader academic life of the College as it is established and grows.
RUA seeks artist-educators who combine strong professional practice with a commitment to high-quality teaching. Ideal candidates will demonstrate:
Industry-active professional practice in their specialist area
The ability to teach at university level using structured syllabi, clear learning outcomes, and assessment approaches
The ability to supervise student productions and creative projects from rehearsal or development through to final presentation
The ability to work across diverse theatrical traditions, including Western and Arabic contexts.
x: A cover letter addressing your suitability for the role and identifying the specialisation you are applying for
relevant professional memberships, awards, and international experience.
A professional portfolio or evidence of creative practice, relevant to your specialist area (see below)
Names and contact details of three referees
Professional Portfolio / Evidence of Creative Practice
Applicants should provide examples of professional work relevant to the position, according to their specialist area:
Acting: showreels, performance credits, recordings of theatre or screen work, or examples of actor training practice
Movement & Choreography: choreographic portfolios, recordings of dance or movement work, and professional performance credits
Directing: directing portfolios, production credits, or documentation of theatre productions, festivals, and live events
Dramaturgy & Dramatic Writing: dramaturgical portfolios, writing samples, script extracts, production credits, or relevant research and publication.
Candidates may provide links rather than uploading large files.

Applications should be submitted to FacultyCareer@rua.edu.sa. Applicants are requested to use the following subject line: Faculty Position, College of Theatre and Performing Arts, [Your Specialization].

d: Zeeco fosters a robust work environment where employees, from engineering teams to support groups, benefit from a strong culture, trained leadership, and opportunities for growth. Zeeco collaborates with the biggest names in the industry, enabling individuals to broaden their skills alongside teams of subject matter experts.

Zeeco is a global leader in combustion and environmental solutions, renowned for our expertise in designing, engineering, and manufacturing advanced burners, incinerators, and environmental control systems. Serving a wide array of industries such as oil and gas, petrochemicals, and power generation, we deliver innovative technologies that enhance operational efficiency, safety, and environmental compliance

We are seeking an experienced Senior Combustion Solutions Consultant to support end users across the refining, petrochemical, and energy sectors. This customer-facing role is focused on combustion systems and fired heater performance, helping customers optimise safety, reliability, efficiency, and environmental compliance.

This opportunity is ideal for a technically strong engineer with extensive fired heater and combustion experience, who enjoys troubleshooting complex operating challenges and delivering practical, value-driven solutions in the field.
q: Significant Oil & Gas, petrochemical, refining, or process industry experience.
Extensive hands-on experience with combustion systems and fired heaters is essential.
Strong knowledge of fired equipment operation, troubleshooting, maintenance, and commissioning.
Mechanical or Process Engineering background preferred.
Proven ability to diagnose combustion-related issues and implement effective solutions.
Excellent customer-facing, communication, and relationship-building skills.
Self-motivated, proactive, and comfortable working independently.
Willingness to travel internationally, including to customer sites and turnaround projects.

This is an excellent opportunity to become a trusted technical advisor, helping customers maximise the performance and reliability of their critical combustion and fired heater assets while supporting the growth of Zeeco's industry-leading solutions.

Working at Zeeco means being part of a people-centric culture and environment built on mutual respect, personal encouragement, professional integrity, and limitless opportunity. Join Zeeco and embark on a fulfilling journey where innovation, collaboration, and personal and professional growth converge.
r: Provide expert technical support for fired heaters, furnaces, boilers, flares, incinerators, and combustion systems.
Diagnose equipment issues, identify root causes, and develop engineered solutions to improve performance and reliability.
Conduct fired heater assessments, condition surveys, pre-turnaround inspections, and commissioning support.
Evaluate equipment integrity, maintenance requirements, and spare parts strategies.
Lead site troubleshooting activities and support customer startups and operational improvements.
Work closely with Zeeco's engineering and product specialists to deliver complete combustion solutions.
Develop strong relationships with existing and prospective customers, identifying opportunities for products and services.
Deliver technical presentations, training, and customer workshops.
Collaborate with sales, engineering, project, and service teams to secure and execute business opportunities.
Travel extensively throughout the region to support customer sites.
